\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Continuous torus pullback is integrable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_gaussianTorusPullback}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_gaussianTorusPullback}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianTorusMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianTorusMap}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let
$p\in[0,\infty]$, and let $F$ be a continuous real-valued function on the torus
$(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}}$. Define a map from $\mathbb R^n$
to this torus by sending $x$ to the point whose coordinate indexed by $(i,0)$ is $x_i$
modulo $1$ and whose coordinate indexed by $(i,1)$ is $\sqrt2 x_i$ modulo $1$. Then the
composition of $F$ with this map belongs to $L^p(\mu)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuous approximation on a Gaussian torus]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_gaussianTorus_approximation}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_gaussianTorus_approximation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuous_gaussianTorusMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianTorusMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.surjective_gaussianTorus_pullback}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\mu$ be a finite measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $p$ be an extended
nonnegative real number with $1\le p<\infty$. If $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belongs to
$L^p(\mu)$, then there is a sequence of continuous real-valued functions on the torus
indexed by $\mathbb N^n\times\{0,1\}$ whose compositions with the map sending $x$ to the
torus point with coordinates $x_i$ and $\sqrt2 x_i$ converge to $f$ in $L^p(\mu)$ and
converge to $f$ pointwise for $\mu$-almost every $x$.
\end{lemma}
